children: New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- Hindustan Copper, Hindustan Zinc, Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Limited, Vedanta, etc are the top metal companies that may emerge as the direct beneficiaries of India's critical mineral push. From cell phones to space technology to manufacturing of cameras, critical minerals have become an increasingly important part of India's economic growth.

"India's critical minerals strategy is no longer just policy ,it is becoming a multi-decade industrial imperative. Budget 2026 dedicated Rare Earth Corridors across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu, while KABIL is actively securing overseas lithium assets in Argentina," explained Gaurav Bhandari, CEO, Monarch Networth Capital.

"Hindustan Zinc, GMDC, Vedanta, NMDC and Hindustan Copper are among the listed Indian companies best positioned to gain from the government's critical-minerals and rare-earth drive, including the National Critical Mineral Mission, the Rs.7,280-crore rare-earth permanent magnet scheme and dedicated mineral corridors," stated Santosh Meena, Head of Research at Swastika Investmart.

Anil Agarwal-led Vedanta offers diversified exposure across zinc, aluminium, and copper but carries higher leverage. Vedanta has secured 10 out of all the 55 critical mineral blocks that were auctioned till October, 2025. It covers critical minerals like cobalt, rare earth elements (REEs), vanadium, graphite and potash. Vedanta stock closed 2.7% lower at Rs.257.2 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.1,00,575.18 crore on Tuesday, September 15.

"Among listed players, Hindustan Copper stands out as the strongest fundamental play ,it is India's only vertically integrated copper miner, sitting on a strategic monopoly as copper demand surges from EVs, renewables, 5G infrastructure, and AI data centres," pointed out Gaurav Bhandari.
Hindustan Copper stock closed 4.34% lower at Rs.492.05 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.47,582.42 crore on Tuesday.

National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) is also a top metal player which is likely to benefit from the expansion of India's critical mineral industry. "NALCO is a close second , its MoUs with NML and BARC for extracting rare earth elements and gallium from red mud could unlock an entirely new revenue stream from what is currently industrial waste," added Gaurav Bhandari.
NALCO stock closed 2.79% lower at Rs.351.3 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.64,520.87 crore on Tuesday, September 15.

"Hindustan Zinc has the strongest near-term case after securing monazite and other critical-mineral blocks and actively diversifying beyond zinc," explained Santosh Meena, Head of Research at Swastika Investmart.

Earlier this year, Hindustan Zinc became one of India's first private players to secure a rare earth (monazite) block, a land-based, non-radioactive deposit distinct. The company scrip closed 2.61% lower at Rs.561 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.2,37,040.40 crore on Tuesday.

Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC) will have the most direct rare earth exposure among state miners and is likely to benefit from active exploration in Gujarat and a low debt balance sheet, as highlighted by Gaurav Bhandari.
GMDC stock closed 3.83% lower Rs.553.15 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.17,590.17 crore on Tuesday.

NMDC while primarily being an iron ore company is diversifying into critical minerals, which also makes it potential beneficiary of the critical minerals industry expansion. NMDC stock closed 2.13% lower at Rs.80.69 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.70,941.18 crore on Tuesday. Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from MINT.
